cases.customer_question: Can transmit output power qualification failures be resolved by modifying DUT firmware power configuration values used during RF PHY testing?
question_variants: Can firmware settings increase RF PHY output power?
How do Int/Ext tester settings affect Bluetooth output power testing?
Can RF PHY failures be fixed by changing FW power parameters?
Should DUT firmware be modified to meet Class 1 power?
Can BlueTest3 power issues be resolved through firmware configuration?
cases.actual_issue: Investigating whether DUT firmware transmit power configuration values and BlueTest3 interface settings caused RF PHY output power failures during Bluetooth qualification testing.
cases.plain_english_explanation: Bluetooth RF test results depend not only on hardware but also on firmware power configuration settings. If the firmware limits transmit power too aggressively, the measured output may fall below qualification requirements. Adjusting firmware parameters can sometimes recover enough output power to pass testing.
cases.consultant_answer: The consultant reviewed the BlueTest3 setup and noted that testing had been performed using the default Int=50 configuration. The consultant requested confirmation of the actual production firmware power setting and suggested that increasing the firmware INT configuration above 50 might raise output power enough to exceed the 10 dBm Class 1 threshold. The consultant proposed retesting using updated firmware configuration values if the customer provided the new settings or firmware update package.
cases.decision_logic: Bluetooth RF PHY output measurements are affected by DUT firmware transmit power configuration. If the production firmware uses different power parameters than the tested configuration, retesting with corrected settings may resolve output power qualification failures.
cases.final_recommendation: Verify the actual production firmware transmit power configuration before RF PHY testing and provide updated firmware or parameter settings to the test lab if output power optimization is required.
cases.risk_if_done_wrong: Testing with incorrect firmware power settings can produce invalid RF PHY evidence, unnecessary failures, repeated retesting, and delayed qualification schedules.
